title: Region-specific storage tiers pricing experiment + Security Questionnaire runbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Run a pricing and packaging experiment that introduces region-specific storage tiers (EU-only, EU+UK, and EU+UK+On-prem connector) combined with an enterprise-facing Security Questionnaire (SQ) response runbook. The goal is to convert mid-sized and enterprise prospects that require explicit residency, SCCs, and retention guarantees into self-servable SKUs or low-touch quotes.

Scope:
- Define 2–3 residency SKUs with clear retention defaults and optional retention add-ons.
- Produce a standard SQ runbook that maps SKU features to canonical security questionnaire answers (subprocessors, retention, KMS, SCCs, audit logs).
- Create quote templates and contract language snippets for common customer asks (SCCs, DPA retention tiers, subprocessors, KMS/HSM).
- Instrument console and sales quote UI to surface SKU selection, exportable SQ answers, and checkbox-able legal concessions.

Hypothesis:
If we offer clear, priced residency SKUs plus a fast SQ response runbook, then sales cycles for customers with moderate data locality needs will shorten and conversion velocity will increase, reducing the number of fully bespoke contract negotiations. Success will be measured by conversion rate lift, reduced legal cycle time, and a decrease in custom contract requests.

Proposed SKUs (experiment A/B):
- Residency Standard (EU storage, 30-day default retention, standard subprocessors; included in hosted pricing with +15% premium)
- Residency Plus (EU+UK storage, configurable retention 30/90/365 days, SCCs pre-attached, optional customer-managed KMS; +40% premium or fixed add-on)
- Residency Connector (EU+UK + on-prem connector option for hybrid customers; quote-only, engineering intake required)

Success metrics (primary/secondary):
- Primary: % increase in MQL->SQL conversion for accounts with residency requirements (target +25% vs historical).
- Primary: Mean time from initial SQ to legal sign-off for customers under $250k ARR (target reduce from 28 days -> 10 days).
- Secondary: # of deals that use SKUs vs custom contracts; average contract negotiation hours saved; incremental ARR from SKU upsell.

Constraints & Trade-offs:
- Engineering effort to ensure traffic/data tagging, region routing, and retention enforcement before public SKU launch (dependent on ENG-5032).
- Some enterprise customers will still require bespoke clauses (encryption attestations, subprocessor exceptions) — expect a residual tail of manual legal work.
- Pricing must reflect capacity & operational cost; higher price may reduce uptake but increases margin and reduces custom-negotiation incentive.

Runbook deliverables (product + legal + security):
- SQ canonical answers document (Drive link) mapping each SKU to 200+ common SQ items (subprocessors, encryption, retention, logging, incident response).
- Template DPA language and SCC attachments for EU/UK that can be auto-included in quotes.
- Sales quote builder snippets (Console + downloadable PDF) and an internal champion checklist for Legal to accelerate approvals.
- Internal gating checklist for engineering readiness (routing tests, audit logs, KMS integration).

Experiment design & rollout plan:
1) Internal pilot: present SKU language + SQ runbook to 3 assigned AE teams and Legal. Collect feedback and iterate (2 weeks).
2) Beta: enable SKUs in Console for new accounts in EU region with an inline SQ export button; A/B test pricing (two price points for Residency Plus). Track acceptance over 8 weeks.
3) Evaluate and iterate: runbook updates, pricing adjustments, and GTM collateral. Decide on GA or extended beta.

Operational notes for engineering:
- ENG tasks: ensure request routing honors customer storage selection, enforce retention at storage layer, and expose per-customer audit logs and subprocessors metadata (ENG-5032, ENG-5187).
- Monitoring: add dashboards for SKU uptake, failed routing events (latency/400s), and retention enforcement audits.

Delivery artifacts & links:
- Confluence working doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/ResidencyPricingDraft (internal)
- SQ canonical answers (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/Residency-SQ-Runbook
- Pricing model spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/Residency-Pricing-Model
- GitHub PR for quote UI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1427

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Legal pushback on automated SCC attachment. Mitigation: Legal-approved clause set and checkbox requiring customer acceptance; escalate to bespoke only if additional clause requested.
- Risk: Engineering delays prevent GA. Mitigation: Beta gating to EU-only and limiting initial retention options to 30/90 days.

Next steps (owners):
- Product (Maya): finalize SKU language and experiment matrix by 2025-02-21.
- Legal (Isha Patel): draft DPA and SCC templates and review SQ runbook by 2025-02-25.
- Security (Leo Martinez): validate SQ canonical answers and KMS options by 2025-02-26.
- Engineering (Oliver Grant lead): implement routing + audit hooks (ENG-5032) scope agreed by 2025-03-01.
